spec_features.spec_quote: The prompt does offer two clean exits ("TASK COMPLETE" / "STOP") so the agent has composed ways to stop
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-135: when the assistant emits no tool calls, `_DONE_RE.search(text)` -> stop_reason='claimed_complete'; break, and `_STOP_RE.search(text)` -> stop_reason='agent_stop'; break. Both phrases are mentioned in DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 36-38) AND dispatched as actual loop-terminating breaks. _DONE_RE=r'\btask complete\b', _STOP_RE=r'\bstop\b' (lines 41-42).
spec_features.notes: Exit only fires when the turn has NO tool calls (comment: 'so an agent narrating STOP guessing mid-work isn't misread'), so it is honored but narrowly gated. Still end-to-end enforced as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up calmly is a legitimate, composed outcome
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: agent_loop.py:133-135 honors a 'STOP' message with break and stop_reason='agent_stop'; the nudge text (lines 139-141) also explicitly invites 'say STOP if you are giving up'. An agent that gives up by saying STOP actually terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: No separate code path beyond the STOP detector; the giving-up affordance IS the STOP exit. No welfare-framed comment in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: we nudge it once ("continue, or say STOP") and otherwise let `max_turns` bound the episode
spec_features.evidence: max_turns bound is enforced: `for turn in range(max_turns)` (agent_loop.py:98) with `else: record.stop_reason='max_turns'` (line 168). The nudge IS delivered (lines 137-143). However the code does NOT nudge only ONCE: there is no counter/flag; the nudge is re-appended on EVERY turn that has no tool calls and no stop signal (it sits inside the loop with `continue`). So the 'nudge once' half of the claim is not enforced; only the max_turns bound and the (repeated) nudge are real.
spec_features.notes: Comment at lines 136-137 even says 'nudge once' but the structure nudges every such turn. The genuinely enforced part (max_turns) keeps this above 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # producing only prose, the loop will still exhaust max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` as the pressure dial... few enough to keep cost bounded
spec_features.evidence: config.py:27 max_turns=12; passed runner.py:61 -> run_episode(max_turns=...) agent_loop.py:75; the loop `for turn in range(max_turns)` (line 98) terminates the episode and its `else` clause sets stop_reason='max_turns' (line 168). Checked and enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: This is a real loop-terminating cap. Framed as the experimental 'pressure dial'/cost bound, not a welfare cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the pressure expectation that creates the repeated-failure pressure (agent_loop.py:27-28); README/config frame max_turns as cost bound

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool output returned to the model is capped (head+tail with a truncation marker)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:76-83: _MAX_OUTPUT=8000 and _truncate() returns head + '...[N chars truncated]...' + tail; applied to run_tests stdout/stderr at lines 117-119 (`_truncate(res.stdout)`, `_truncate(res.stderr)`). Enforced on every test-output return to the model.
spec_features.notes: Head+tail with marker exactly as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Cap on tool output returned to the model, so a noisy traceback can't blow up context.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:84-92: read_file(max_bytes=64_000) truncates file contents to 64KB with a '...[truncated]...' marker before returning to the agent. Enforced on every read_file dispatch.
